title: Patch: the AI tries a lane-minded card in every lane, not only the two leftmost
thread:
**Issue #1635 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #1635: Patch: the AI tries a lane-minded card in every lane, not only the two leftmost
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Some cards care where they land. Lane Eater destroys everything else in its lane, Mushroom Power buffs the Units beside it, and Joon Jorker buffs the Unit to its right. When the practice AI considers playing a card, it only tries the first two distinct spots counting from the left. So with the opponent's big Taunt in lane 4, the AI never even considers dropping Lane Eater into lane 4 to destroy it. Once this is built, the AI looks at every distinct lane for the play it is about to make, and these cards land where they do their job. Players notice the AI using lane cards like a person would.

## Why
- `collapse_zones` (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:98-115`) keeps, for each otherwise identical play, the first `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants` distinct placements in lane order.
- `zone_variants` is 2 (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:140`). Its doc (`config.rs:74-77`) says 3 "let a Tribute play's sets outgrow the lethal allowance".
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs:330-341` pins this: with a unit opposite every lane, only lanes 1 and 2 are offered.
- Cards whose text reads their own lane or neighbours (`crates/cards/catalog.json`):
  - Lane Eater `classic-071`: "Cry: Destroy every other card in this lane. Lock this lane."
  - Mushroom Power `classicplus-020`: "Cry: Give the Units adjacent to this +{buff}/+{buff}."
  - Joon Jorker `meditative-061`: "End of turn: Buff the Unit to the right of this …"
  - Bunker `meditative-097-5`: "This strikes Units in its lane with {multiplier}× its Attack."
- `score_line` (`crates/ai/src/search.rs:231-245`) cuts a finalist's line at the first action missing from that world's `candidate_set`. A wider root therefore has to widen the membership check too, or a finalist in lanes 3 to 5 is cut on every other world.

## Proposal
At the search root only, keep every distinct placement instead of the first two. That covers the beam's first expansion and `score_line`'s membership check for a line's first action. Deeper levels, the lethal solver and the opponent's reply keep `zone_variants`, which is what #1014's cap protects. The root's branching cap (`AI_BUDGET.root_branching`, 20) and the node budget stay as they are.

## Where it lands
- `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs` (`collapse_zones` and its root caller), `crates/ai/src/search.rs`
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs`: the `zone_variants` doc says where the cap applies
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs`
- SPEC §9.9 if it names the cap

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Search test, failing today: p1 holds Lane Eater with the mana to play it, and p2 has Midrange Menace `core-019` (9/9 Taunt) in lane 4 and nothing else. The root candidates include the play into lane 4, and in that position `decide` makes it.
- [ ] Mushroom Power with p1's Units in lanes 3 and 5: lane 4 is a root candidate. It is not today.
- [ ] `search.rs`'s collapse test now says the root keeps every placement and a deeper level keeps `zone_variants`. One test pins the lethal solver's and the reply's candidate sets as unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai --test ai_slow`, clippy and `cargo jackioh gate` pass. The change is screened on the dev set as `training/improve.md` says, and the result is in the pull request.

## Size and risks
About 25 lines and 3 tests. It is AI work, so hard. The node count per decision does not change, but extra placements can push other moves out of the root's 20 branches. That is the main thing the screen measures. If it costs strength, ordering the extra placements behind the first two is a fallback that keeps lane cards reachable.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

Class: `ai` → `priority:low`; relabel to change it.

<!-- jackioh-bot -->

---
Comment by @MaxGoetzmann at 2026-10-22T14:58:16Z:

Approve
```

## Goal

At the search's root only, the AI tries each play in every distinct placement instead of the first `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants` (2). The beam's first expansion, `score_line`'s check of a line's first action and `policy_label` (which labels root decisions) read new root lists. Deeper beam levels, the lethal solver, the opponent's reply, `decide`'s probe and the baselines keep `zone_variants`. It is done when these tests pass, the practice-claim fixture is re-recorded and the dev-set screen's result is recorded:

- Lane Eater facing Midrange Menace in lane 4: the root offers lane 4 and `decide` plays it.
- Mushroom Power with p1's Units in lanes 3 and 5: the root offers lane 4.
- The collapse test says the root keeps every placement and a deeper level keeps `zone_variants`.
- One test pins the lethal solver's and the reply's lists as unchanged.

13. **Screen** (training/improve.md, "A screen"): run `cargo jackioh arena --a self --b bin:~/control-jackioh --set improve-dev` (400 games). In `root_candidate_actions`, emit `candidate_actions(state, seat)` minus its trailing `EndTurn`, then the plays of `root_candidate_set` that are not in it, in their `root_candidate_set` order, then `EndTurn` when it is a candidate.     - If that also has `edgeHigh` < 0, ship it anyway and say so plainly in the report.

## Tests

In `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs`. The planner ran each of these on a prototype of exactly these steps, and they pass. Copy the existing `lane_eater_is_tried_opposite_the_enemy_taunt_and_decide_plays_it_there` (line 602) for scenario shape and the `decide` assertion.

- `mod candidate_actions_b14`, rename `b14_a_play_keeps_the_lowest_lane_of_each_placement_and_none_past_the_cap` to `b14_a_play_keeps_the_lowest_lane_of_each_placement_every_one_at_the_root_none_past_the_cap_deeper`. Doc: "B14: a play keeps the lowest lane of each placement: every one at the search's root (#1635), none past AI_SEARCH.zone_variants deeper (#1014)". Keep both of today's assertions, with `crowded_row()` in place of the inline literal, and add:
  - `root_offered_lanes(&empty, "core-008") == vec![1, 2, 5]`;
  - `root_offered_lanes(&crowded, "core-008") == vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`;
  - `play_lanes(&root_expansion(&crowded, AI, AI_BUDGET.root_branching, MoveOrder::Heuristic, &POLICY_PRIOR)) == vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`;

    - `decide(&state, AI, &mut ai_options("search-lane-eater-4", AI_BUDGET))` returns a Play of the Lane Eater's hand id with `zone.lane == 4`.
  - `score_line_replays_a_first_action_only_the_root_offers`:
    - the lane-4 play is `root_candidate_actions(&state, AI)`'s action with `lane_of == Some(4)`;
    - `counter = create_node_counter(AI_BUDGET.nodes, None)`;
    - `score_line(&state, AI, &[play], &counter, false, None)` must be greater than `score_line(&state, AI, &[], &counter, false, None)`. Before step 3 the play is cut and both scores are equal.

```
cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai search::
cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai policy::
```

## Done when

- [ ] Root lists exist and are used only at depth 0, in `score_line`'s first action and in `policy_label`. Every other caller is unchanged.
- [ ] The five tests above pass, and the Lane Eater, Mushroom and score_line tests fail on `main`.
- [ ] `crates/server/tests/fixtures/practice-claim.json` is re-recorded, the server's r1303002 test passes and `claim.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] The AI crate's lib, ai and ai_slow tests, the full workspace tests, clippy, fmt, `gate` and `classify --claims` all pass.
- [ ] The screen's line is in `config.rs` and in the report, and the step 13 rule is applied.

## Risks

- **The root's 20 branches.** Extra placements come after every source's first two variants (`round_robin`), but before trades that are not kills, answers and switches. In a wide hand they can push those out of the root. The screen measures this, and step 13 has the fallback.
- **The node budget is unchanged.** `decide`'s probe stays on `candidate_actions`, so `fat_width`, and with it the scaled budget, are as before. The forced check is unchanged too: a single capped candidate means there was only one placement.
- **Determinism and hidden information** hold. `placement_key` reads only what the seat can see (R185), and nothing draws on an rng.
- **The beam still collapses plain lanes.** `search_signature` (simulate.rs, line 835) leaves a unit's lane out. A plain unit's extra lanes still collapse into one child, and only the nodes are spent. A card whose payoff comes later, Joon Jorker's end-of-turn buff, is collapsed the same way. That is out of scope: say so in the report.
- **Pinned AI play.** On the prototype only the practice-claim fixture moved. If another pinned game fails (the tutorial tier, the puzzles, the gate's smoke), report it by name. Never loosen it.

## Open questions

- None block the build. Only a person can decide whether a screen whose interval straddles 0 is enough to ship; step 13 ships it, as the issue asks for behaviour, not strength.

````markdown
## Risks

- **The root's 20 branches.** Extra placements come after every source's first two variants (`round_robin`), but before trades that are not kills, answers and switches. In a wide hand they can push those out of the root. The screen measures this, and step 13 has the fallback.
- **The node budget is unchanged.** `decide`'s probe stays on `candidate_actions`, so `fat_width`, and with it the scaled budget, are as before. The forced check is unchanged too: a single capped candidate means there was only one placement.
- **Determinism and hidden information** hold. `placement_key` reads only what the seat can see (R185), and nothing draws on an rng.
- **The beam still collapses plain lanes.** `search_signature` (simulate.rs, line 835) leaves a unit's lane out. A plain unit's extra lanes still collapse into one child, and only the nodes are spent. A card whose payoff comes later, Joon Jorker's end-of-turn buff, is collapsed the same way. That is out of scope: say so in the report.
- **Pinned AI play.** On the prototype only the practice-claim fixture moved. If another pinned game fails (the tutorial tier, the puzzles, the gate's smoke), report it by name. Never loosen it.

## Open questions

- None block the build. Only a person can decide whether a screen whose interval straddles 0 is enough to ship; step 13 ships it, as the issue asks for behaviour, not strength.
````
